title: Rigveda 5.84: Earth
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.84: Earth: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.84 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to earth. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 398r-398v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.84.1 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 398r
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>baḻ i̱tthā parva̍tānāṁ khi̱dram bi̍bharṣi pṛthivi | pra yā bhūmi̍m pravatvati ma̱hnā ji̱noṣi̍ mahini ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>THOU, of a truth,O Pr̥ithivî, bearest the tool that rends the hills: Thou rich in torrents, who with might quickenest earth, O Mighty One.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 398r (numbered 71r by the scribe) (OPenn image 398, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.83.8 ‹-kulyāḥ vi-sitāḥ purastāt ghṛtena›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 398v (numbered 71v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.84.2 ‹heṣantam perum asyasi arjuni›. Verse 5.84.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>baṭ | itthā | parvatānām | khidram | bibharṣi | pṛthivi | pra | yā | bhūmim | pravatvati | mahnā | jinoṣi | mahini

translation.original_ref: RV 5.84.2-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 398v
translation.original_text:
2stomā̍sas tvā vicāriṇi̱ prati̍ ṣṭobhanty a̱ktubhi̍ḥ | pra yā vāja̱ṁ na heṣa̍ntam pe̱rum asya̍sy arjuni ||
3dṛ̱ḻhā ci̱d yā vana̱spatī̍n kṣma̱yā dardha̱rṣy oja̍sā | yat te̍ a̱bhrasya̍ vi̱dyuto̍ di̱vo varṣa̍nti vṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
2To thee, O wanderer at will, ring out the lauds with beams of day, Who drivest, like a neighing steed, the swelling cloud, O bright of hue.
3Who graspest with thy might on earth. e'en the strong sovrans of the wood, When from the lightning of thy cloud the rain-floods of the heaven descend.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 398v (numbered 71v by the scribe) (OPenn image 399, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.84.2 ‹heṣantam perum asyasi arjuni›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 399r (numbered 72r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.85.3 ‹rājā yavam na vṛṣṭiḥ›. Verses 5.84.2-3 end on this page; 5.84.2 begins on fol. 398r (numbered 71r by the scribe).

3dṛḷhā | cit | yā | vanaspatīn | kṣmayā | dardharṣi | ojasā | yat | te | abhrasya | vi-dyutaḥ | divaḥ | varṣanti | vṛṣṭayaḥ
